title: Questions players ask most
summary: Short, checkable answers to the questions this site is asked most about running the shop, each one pointing at the entry that explains it in full rather than repeating it here.
body: These are the questions that come up most, answered in a sentence or two. Every answer is backed by something the game itself defines, and the longer explanation sits in the entry named beside it.
On opening packs: a pack can be opened by hand or by a machine, and the build keeps the machine's save record as its own thing, so an automatic opener is a fixture you own rather than a setting.
On cards you cannot sell: there is a bulk donation box with its own screen, and customers arrive wanting to use it, so unwanted cards have somewhere to go other than the bin.
On customers: some arrive specifically to trade cards or to buy a card, and those wants are named separately from the wants for goods, which is why the customer entries split them apart.
On pricing: a price tag is a physical fixture in the build, with its own screen and its own picture sheet, so prices are changed at the shelf rather than in one master list.
On money: the shop tracks more than one currency, and the game names eight of them, which is why takings and prices carry a currency rather than a bare number.
On your workers: a worker can be given a main job and a second job, and some jobs run on their own once set, which is why staff are described as assigned rather than commanded.
What this list does not do is guess. Where an answer would need a number we have not verified, we say so rather than inventing one.

facts.claim: A pack can be opened by a machine the shop owns, and the machine keeps its own save record.
There is a bulk donation box with its own screen, and customers arrive wanting to use it.
Some customers arrive to trade a card or to buy a specific card, separately from ordinary wants.
A price tag is a physical fixture with its own screen and its own picture sheet.
The shop tracks more than one currency, and the game names eight of them.
A worker can be given a main job and a second job, and some jobs then run on their own.
Storage shelves remember what was taken from them rather than only how full they are.
The build ships a question-mark icon of its own, which is the picture the game draws for a question.
